evidence: src/domain/DomainErrors.ts: InvalidValueError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidTransitionError all extend DomainError; Order.ts, OrderLine.ts, Product.ts and StockAllocationService.ts raise these errors

src/domain/OrderStatus.ts: FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE_STATUSES, nextStatus() and isCancellable() are the only place the lifecycle rules are defined; Order.advanceTo and Order.cancel call them instead of re-encoding them

src/domain/OrderRepository.ts and src/domain/ProductRepository.ts: interfaces defined over the module's own Order and Product aggregates
Minor overlap: OrderLine.of and Product.ts assertPositiveInteger both check Number.isInteger(q) && q > 0; this is a small input guard, not a split business rule
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one concern: order fulfilment and stock allocation. Its files use the module's abstractions consistently. One error hierarchy (DomainError) is used everywhere. The order lifecycle rules live only in OrderStatus.ts and Order uses them. Merging lines for the same product lives only in OrderLine.consolidate. StockAllocationService changes stock only through Product's public methods and never alters Product state directly. The repository interfaces are defined over the module's own aggregates. One small duplication exists: the positive-integer quantity check appears in both OrderLine.of and Product's assertPositiveInteger. It is a minor input guard, not a business invariant split across files, so it does not make the module fail.
